paths.description: Homepage and live-score listing, representing the primary core journey.
France vs England match detail, representing live event detail, tabs, rich data, and app promotion.
World Championship tournament detail, representing standings and competition navigation.
News listing, representing editorial content and a distinct template.
Unknown route, representing HTTP or routing failure handling.

findings.summary: Motion continues under reduced-motion
findings.evidence: Three animations remain running under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, with 800 to 1000 ms durations.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential transitions and infinite animation in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query.

findings.summary: High-contrast preference is not applied across the app
findings.evidence: Only third-party sign-in styles respond to prefers-contrast, while axe records contrast as low as 1.82:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add app-wide prefers-contrast and forced-colors treatment and verify every control in forced-colors mode.

findings.summary: Route and state changes omit View Transitions
findings.evidence: Stylesheet inspection found no view-transition rules on home or match detail.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document and cross-document View Transitions for major route and tab changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Fixed navigation does not react to scroll state
findings.evidence: The app has persistent top and bottom chrome but no scroll-state queries or scroll timelines.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a declarative progress treatment to reduce chrome and preserve context while scrolling.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures every primary path on first load
findings.evidence: Home, match, tournament, and news screenshots are all covered by a nearly full-viewport consent dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize the first layer, preserve access to core content, and provide clear accept and reject choices without obscuring the journey.

findings.summary: Overlays use custom role=dialog DIVs
findings.evidence: DOM inspection identifies consent and promotional overlays as DIV elements with role=dialog rather than native dialog or popover.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, with declarative close and focus behavior.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inadequate
findings.evidence: The focused score link computed outline style none, and many visible links are only 14 to 16 CSS pixels high.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible indicator and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, preferably 44 by 44 for touch.

findings.summary: Primary score and content journeys are interrupted
findings.evidence: Every representative journey requires dealing with the consent wall before core content can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep core public content usable while presenting a compact, reversible privacy choice.

findings.summary: Core load performance is far outside the good range
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 22.4 s LCP, 860 ms TBT, 8.0 s Speed Index, and performance 0.44.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP chain, prioritize its resource, reduce hydration work, and defer non-critical third-party code.

findings.summary: Match detail has severe layout shift
findings.evidence: The 360px match path measured CLS 0.641, including a 0.467 shift near 5.65 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late match, ad, and consent content; add intrinsic image sizing and stable font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Main-thread work delays interactivity
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 860 ms TBT and traces observed long tasks up to 117 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks into prioritized chunks and defer analytics, ads, and below-fold rendering.

findings.summary: Initial delivery is excessively heavy
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 409 requests and 4.27 MB transferred, with 92 scripts and 272 image requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce request fan-out, prioritize only critical scripts and images, and defer below-fold and third-party resources.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused code ship on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 686 KiB unused JavaScript and 76 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route-specific bundles, conditionally load ads and identity code, and remove unused CSS from the initial route.

findings.summary: Core controls have invalid or missing accessible semantics
findings.evidence: axe found unnamed buttons, an unlabeled switch, invalid aria-selected attributes, and a scrollbar missing aria-valuenow.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control an accessible name, use the correct tab or option roles, label the odds switch, and replace the invalid scrollbar role.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail WCAG contrast
findings.evidence: axe measured 3.43:1 for live-state text and 1.82:1 in the consent UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust semantic color tokens to meet WCAG AA in every theme and consent state.

findings.summary: Landmarks and keyboard focus are unreliable
findings.evidence: axe found content outside landmarks and nested interactive controls; the focused link had no visible outline style.
findings.suggestedFix: Contain page regions in landmarks, remove nested interactive semantics, and add a persistent :focus-visible ring.

findings.summary: Many visible targets are too short
findings.evidence: The target probe found many score and competition links only 14 to 16 CSS pixels high despite successful reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas without changing visual density, using padding and pseudo-element target expansion.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured failed resources and an uncaught TypeError while reading stages during migration.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the migration guard and handle expected API failures without console errors.

findings.summary: Most images lack intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: The image audit found 98 of 100 images without width and height and 32 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and request the closest available image size.

findings.summary: A persistent WebSocket blocks BFCache
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports that the page cannot enter back-forward cache because of its WebSocket.
findings.suggestedFix: Close or suspend the live connection on pagehide and reconnect on pageshow where the browser permits.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript and AI crawler access is blocked
findings.evidence: The raw fetch returned HTTP 403 with zero coverage, and robots.txt blocks Bytespider.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful server-rendered HTML to legitimate crawlers and review AI crawler policy against content-discovery goals.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: HSTS is missing, CSP only has frame-ancestors, and FCCDCF is not Secure while SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, deploy a nonce or hash based script CSP, and set Secure on every SameSite=None cookie.

findings.summary: The first load has a large tracking and partner footprint
findings.evidence: Ten third-party origins load, known ad trackers are active, and the consent UI names 357 partners plus precise geolocation.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and purposes, load optional partners only after choice, and batch essential analytics.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are incomplete
findings.evidence: HSTS and Referrer-Policy are absent, while CSP protects only against framing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, a restrictive Referrer-Policy, script-src enforcement, and Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive sinks.

findings.summary: Core public content is unavailable to the raw client
findings.evidence: The raw response was a 48-byte HTTP 403 with zero overlap against 8,974 rendered text characters.
findings.suggestedFix: Return server-rendered core scores and metadata, then hydrate enhancements without making JavaScript or crawler classification a content gate.

findings.summary: The installable app has no evidenced offline fallback
findings.evidence: A standalone manifest exists, but no service-worker controller or registration was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker and provide an offline shell with a clear stale or reconnect state for recent scores.

findings.summary: Consent has no first-layer reject choice
findings.evidence: The modal presents Consent and Manage options, but no equally immediate Reject action, while describing 357 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept and Reject with equal prominence and make granular management optional rather than required for refusal.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bandwidth and layout stability
findings.evidence: The image audit found 84 below-fold images without lazy loading, 32 oversized images, and 98 missing intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold images, use size-specific endpoints or srcset, and emit intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: The initial route performs substantial avoidable work
findings.evidence: The page makes 409 requests, loads 92 scripts, and ships an estimated 686 KiB of unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential data, ads, identity, and below-fold component code until user intent or idle time.

findings.summary: Third parties consume most transferred bytes
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 282 requests and 2.51 MB, about 59% of transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, self-host essential assets, and delay ad, identity, and consent-vendor code until needed.

findings.summary: Initial memory footprint is disproportionate
findings.evidence: The baseline snapshot reported 1,456,507 V8 nodes and 78.9 MB self size before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize long score lists, avoid rendering hidden responsive variants, and defer below-fold trees.
